items.headline: Cell therapies: breaking barriers in solid tumours
items.preview: New advancements in cancer cell therapies aim to tackle solid tumours more effectively.
items.article:
It's been nearly a decade since the first CAR-T cancer cell therapy was approved by the FDA, offering a powerful and durable therapy against tumours. However, CAR-Ts have limitations when it comes to solid tumours. A new generation of cancer cell therapies could set new standards and change the way we think about drug delivery in solid tumours.
Why this matters: The evolution of cell therapies is crucial for improving treatment options for solid tumours, which represent the majority of cancer cases. The challenges faced by CAR-T therapies highlight the need for innovative approaches to enhance efficacy and safety in this area.

items.headline: New Immune Checkpoint Discovery Explains Why Gastric Cancers Ignore PD-1 Drugs
items.preview: A study reveals a mechanism behind gastric cancer's resistance to PD-1 immunotherapy.
items.article:
Researchers have developed a genetically engineered mouse model of gastric cancer that mimics the human disease's characteristics, including resistance to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. The study identifies a molecular circuit involving the oncogenic co-activator YAP and the protein BST2, which reprograms immune cells to become immunosuppressive.
Why this matters: Understanding the mechanisms of resistance in gastric cancer can lead to new therapeutic strategies that enhance the effectiveness of immunotherapies, potentially improving outcomes for patients with this aggressive cancer.

items.headline: BrainStorm Therapeutics combines brain organoids and AI for CNS drug discovery
items.preview: BrainStorm Therapeutics utilizes AI and brain organoids to enhance drug discovery for CNS disorders.
items.article:
BrainStorm Therapeutics is leveraging patient-derived human brain organoids combined with artificial intelligence to improve drug discovery for neurological diseases. This innovative approach aims to identify therapeutic targets and screen drug candidates effectively.
Why this matters: By integrating AI with human biology, BrainStorm aims to enhance the translation of laboratory discoveries into clinical applications, potentially leading to more effective treatments for conditions like CDKL5 deficiency disorder, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's diseases.

items.headline: Coordinated P450–UGT detoxification contributes to furanocoumarin tolerance in Helicoverpa
items.preview: Study reveals how coordinated detoxification mechanisms in insects contribute to plant tolerance.
items.article:
Research on Helicoverpa armigera has uncovered a cooperative detoxification mechanism involving cytochrome P450 and UDP-glycosyltransferase enzymes that enables tolerance to furanocoumarins. This study highlights the evolutionary adaptations of herbivorous insects to plant chemical defenses.
Why this matters: Understanding these detoxification pathways can inform strategies for pest management and crop protection, as they reveal how insects adapt to diverse plant toxins.

items.headline: Antibodies targeting phage proteins impair Acinetobacter baumannii phage therapy
items.preview: Study shows how antibodies against phage proteins can hinder phage therapy effectiveness.
items.article:
A study investigating the effects of antibodies on phage therapy for Acinetobacter baumannii reveals that antibodies targeting the fiber and nozzle proteins of phage AbP20 can block infection and promote immune clearance, leading to therapy failure. This highlights the complex interactions between phage therapy and the host immune response.
Why this matters: Understanding the role of antibodies in phage therapy can help optimize treatment strategies and improve the efficacy of phage-based therapies against antibiotic-resistant infections.
